description.value: A PET study examined the effects of heroin administration and heroin-related visual cues on regional cerebral blood flow in male heroin addicts, including their interaction and a psychophysiological interaction with midbrain activity.

spans.text: The present study was designed to explore the relevance of these findings in real life situations by studying heroin addicts during exposure to both drug-salient cues and heroin.

value: We predicted that heroin exposure would result in activation of the mesolimbic dopamine system.

value: Heroin administration resulted in significant activation in the midbrain within an area centred on the periaqueductal grey but extending to include regions such as VTA and dorsal raphe.
An effect of heroin in this region can be explained as a direct unconditioned effect of the drug in an area known to be rich in opiate receptors.

value: The salient drug video compared with the neutral video resulted in activation in similar and overlapping brain midbrain regions to those of heroin itself.

The fact that pharmacological challenge and salient visual stimulation activate similar brain systems is congruent with predictions from theoretical accounts of value-dependent reinforcement learning.
Strikingly, the visual drug cue elicited a neural response similar to that of heroin.
